title: Vipul Misra appointed acting CEO of SriLankan Airlines
byline: Vipul Misra has been appointed as the acting Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of SriLankan Airlines, effective today (9).

title: Italian Naval vessel ‘ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi’ in Colombo
byline: The Italian Naval Vessel ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi arrived at the Port of Colombo on a replenishment visit to Sri Lanka.

title: School bags to be lighter under new education module system: PM
byline: Schoolchildren will soon have lighter school bags with the introduction of a new modular education system, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

title: Trump offers US$5,000 to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
byline: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (Sep 9) that he would pay every American adult a US$5,000 ’’Trump dividend’’ if Republicans retain control of Congress in November’s midterm election, a striking attempt to persuade voters to back his party.

title: MR meets new Chinese Ambassador
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa held a cordial meeting with newly appointed Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Wei Huaxiang yesterday (9) at his residence in Colombo.

title: India, Sri Lanka discuss defence cooperation
byline: A high-level Indian defence delegation met Sri Lanka’s Deputy Minister of Defence, Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd), at the Ministry of Defence yesterday, during Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s official visit to Sri Lanka.

title: Catholic Bishops call for impartial probe into Chemmani mass graves
byline: The Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Sri Lanka has called for an impartial investigation into the mass graves discovered in the Jaffna Peninsula, stressing that the long-running excavations at Chemmani must be completed to establish the truth and ensure accountability.

title: 22 injured as Colombo-bound bus plunges into canal in Minneriya
byline: Twenty-two passengers were injured after a private bus travelling from Medirigiriya to Colombo veered off the road and overturned into a canal in Minneriya early today (10).

title: Suspect arrested over alleged $80 Mn illegal foreign transfer
byline: A 34-year-old man has been arrested in the Maradana area in connection with an alleged illegal foreign money-transfer operation involving approximately US$80 million, police said.

title: Apple debuts iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
byline: Apple today announced iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, delivering the most advanced pro camera system in an iPhone, and huge leaps in battery life and performance. The new 48MP Fusion Main camera, now with variable aperture, brings creative control that wasn’t possible before, and new Pro controls let users customize their experience in the Camera app.

title: Why Sri Lanka is one of Asia’s most underrated countries, says world traveller Cameron
byline: Sri Lanka is one of the most underrated countries in Asia, according to world traveller Cameron, who praised the island’s natural beauty, wildlife, food, historic sites and hospitality in an interview published on Instagram.

title: Protesters outside mistake Pakistan U19 cricket team for asylum seekers
byline: A group of masked agitators gathered outside a four-star hotel in Portsmouth after reports a group of asylum seekers had been taken there, when it was in fact Pakistan’s under-19 cricket team on a tour.

title: Thennekumbura traders protest against govt., allege JVP supporters favored
byline: Traders in Thennekumbura, Kandy, staged a protest against the government following the removal of roadside stalls under a court order, alleging that supporters of the governing JVP were given preferential treatment during the clearance operation.

title: At least five killed, 87 missing after ferry fire in Philippines
byline: At least five people were killed and 87 remain unaccounted for after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan, the coast guard said Thursday.

title: Aircraft purchase commissions must be accepted, deal becomes void if rejected: Prof. Sonal
byline: The commission paid to the buyer is included in the price of an aircraft, and an aircraft purchase transaction could become null and void if the buyer refuses to accept the commission, former Airport and Aviation Services Company Limited (AASL) Board Director Professor Sonal Fernando said.

title: Sheikh Hasina’s daughter Saima Wazed quits WHO amid fraud allegations
byline: Saima Wazed, the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) Southeast Asia regional director and daughter of ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, resigned from her post on Wednesday amid fraud investigations by the UN health agency and Bangladeshi authorities, Reuters reported, citing her resignation letter.

title: Former Bandarawela Mayor arrested over alleged financial fraud
byline: Former Mayor of the Bandarawela Municipal Council Janaka Nishantha Ratnayake has been arrested in connection with an ongoing investigation into alleged financial fraud and the forgery of documents at the municipal council.

title: 70-year-olds who can’t care for themselves still behind bars
byline: A number of prisoners aged over 70 who are unable to attend to even their basic personal needs remain behind bars, MP Chaminda Wijesiri told Parliament yesterday.

title: Speaker threatens to remove MP from chambers
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today threatened to remove MP Dayasiri Jayasekera from the chamber after the latter protested against a ruling by the Speaker.

title: Sri Lanka calls for end to ‘indefinite’ UN human rights mandates
byline: Sri Lanka has urged UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk to ensure that country-specific human rights mandates are not allowed to continue indefinitely, calling for periodic reviews and clear mechanisms to bring them to an end when countries demonstrate progress.

title: Extreme weather puts Sri Lanka’s unique wildlife and ecosystems at risk
byline: Sri Lanka’s unique wildlife, plants and ecosystems are facing growing pressure from extreme weather, with droughts, floods, landslides, rising temperatures and changing rainfall patterns posing serious challenges to species that depend on fragile and limited habitats.

title: We learnt of US concerns from the Daily Mirror only’ — Iranian Embassy
byline: Amid reports about the presence of Iranian vessels in international waters outside Sri Lanka and the U.S. Embassy raising concerns about it, the Iranian Embassy yesterday said that it had learnt of such concerns only from the Sri Lankan media.

title: Are you using condoms correctly?
byline: Health officials are urging people to use condoms correctly and consistently to reduce the risk of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections (STIs), while warning against the use of substandard condoms.

title: Apple announces first-ever foldable iPhone, starting at $1,999
byline: Apple announced its first-ever foldable iPhone at its annual products event on Wednesday as customers worldwide watched for fresh products, as well as the debut of Apple CEO John Ternus.

title: Supreme Court invalidates presidential pardon granted to Gnanasara Thera
byline: The Supreme Court today ruled that former President Maithripala Sirisena’s decision to grant a presidential pardon to Bodu Bala Sena (BBS) General Secretary Ven. Galagoda Atte Gnanasara Thera was arbitrary and invalid in law.

title: Former Air Chief, astrologer Sumanadasa summoned over probes
byline: Former Commander of the Sri Lanka Air Force, Air Chief Marshal Roshan Goonetileke, arrived at the Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID) this morning (10).

title: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh departs Sri Lanka
byline: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has left the island after concluding his official three-day visit to Sri Lanka.

title: Sri Lanka men’s cricket team to tour Pakistan in October
byline: The Sri Lanka National Men’s Cricket Team is set to tour Pakistan in October and November 2026 for a multi-format series featuring T20 Internationals, an ODI Tri-Nation Series and two Test matches.

title: Rajnath Singh meets Sri Lankan cricket legends
byline: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lankan cricket legends Aravinda de Silva, Sanath Jayasuriya and Chaminda Vaas during his visit to Colombo.

title: Yemen’s Houthis close in on stranglehold over strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait
byline: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of the historic port city of Mocha on Thursday, four Yemeni government military sources said, gaining further leverage over the ​Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

title: Sri Lanka targets stronger position in global supply chains
byline: The 8th Colombo International Maritime and Logistics Conference (CIMC 2026) commenced in Colombo on September 9, bringing together local and international stakeholders to discuss Sri Lanka’s potential to strengthen its position as a key regional maritime and logistics hub.

title: Iran war won’t end until after crucial November elections, says Trump
byline: US President Donald Trump has said he does not think the Iran war will end until after November’s midterm elections, adding that oil prices will not come down until then.

title: Rs. 400,000 fine for selling non-SLS extension cords
byline: A company operating a shopping centre in Bandarawela was fined Rs. 400,000 after pleading guilty to four charges relating to the sale of electrical extension cords without the mandatory SLS certification, the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) said.

title: Traders express anger over removal of fish stalls at Dewata Beach
byline: Traders at Dewata Beach in Galle have expressed strong dissatisfaction following the removal of their fish stalls by the Coastal Conservation Department this morning.

title: Are Ministers behind USD 2.5 million theft, asks Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa said today that some senior Ministers sitting in the two front rows of Parliament may have been behind the alleged theft of USD 2.5 million.

title: Parliament to debate 22A on September 24 and 25
byline: Parliament is scheduled to hold a two-day debate on the proposed 22nd Amendment on September 24 and 25, following a decision reached by party leaders today, the Parliament Media Unit said.

title: Sheikh Hasina’s daughter Saima Wazed quits WHO amid fraud allegations
byline: Saima Wazed, the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) Southeast Asia regional director and daughter of ousted Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, resigned from her post on Wednesday amid fraud investigations by the UN health agency and Bangladeshi authorities, Reuters reported, citing her resignation letter.

title: Malagamuwa denies allegations over Rs.2.5bn property
byline: Sri Lankan racing driver Dilantha Malagamuwa has denied allegations linking him to an alleged land fraud involving a property at Barnes Place, Colombo 7, saying the accusations against him are false and baseless.

title: AG to take action against prosecution witness over alleged false evidence in Yoshitha Rajapaksa case
byline: The Attorney General informed the Colombo High Court today that legal action would be taken against a prosecution witness who allegedly gave false evidence in the money laundering case filed against Yoshitha Rajapaksa, the son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa.

title: Twenty-five dead after fire on cargo ship in eastern China
byline: Twenty-five people have been killed in a fire on a foreign-flagged cargo ship docked at a port in eastern China, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

title: Sri Lanka secures international cooperation through UNCCD summit
byline: Sri Lanka has secured several opportunities for international cooperation in environmental protection, agriculture and trade following the participation of Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi at the Summit of Heads of State of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) in Mongolia.

title: Bambalapitiya Railway Station gets Rs. 60 million facelift
byline: The newly renovated Bambalapitiya Railway Station was officially opened to the public today (10), under the “Dream Destination” initiative aimed at upgrading 100 railway stations under the national “Clean Sri Lanka” programme.

title: Catholic leaders warn of environmental destruction
byline: The Government held discussions with Catholic religious leaders on measures that could be taken to prevent environmental damage and destruction that could adversely affect people’s lives.

title: Jeff Timmons arrives for charity concert
byline: American musician, singer and songwriter Jeff Timmons, founder of the 98 Degrees Foundation, arrived at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake yesterday evening (9) to participate in a charity music concert in Colombo.

title: ACJU calls for justice for Easter Sunday attack victims
byline: Representatives of the All Ceylon Jamiyyathul Ulama (ACJU) called for justice for the victims of the Easter Sunday attacks and urged that information about those responsible be revealed.

title: President warns against hate speech while defending democratic criticism
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said people have the democratic right to question the actions and decisions of the Government, but warned that such freedom should not be used to spread hatred between ethnic communities.

title: ’He’s massive!’ Meet Hugo, the world’s tallest horse
byline: A Shire horse that has entered the record books as the world’s tallest living horse could exceed his height as he is still growing, his owner has said.

title: Preschool development programme planned islandwide by 2027
byline: Islandwide preschool development activities are planned to be implemented by 2027 under Sri Lanka’s new Early Childhood Curriculum Framework and Teacher Guidelines.

title: Restaurant fined for overpricing bottled drinking water
byline: A restaurant in Valachchenai has been fined Rs.750,000 for selling a one-litre bottle of drinking water at Rs.130, exceeding the maximum retail price of Rs.100 prescribed by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA).

title: Don’t play parts played in films in real life, Magistrate warns actor Hemal Ranasinghe
byline: Popular actor Hemal Ranasinghe, who admitted to charges over the assault and criminal intimidation of film critic Lakmina Ranasinghe, was released after the Mount Lavinia Magistrate’s Court accepted a settlement reached between the two parties today.

title: Government plans programmes to reduce migrant worker deaths
byline: The Government is planning awareness and support programmes aimed at reducing the number of Sri Lankan migrant workers who die while employed overseas, Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: New education reforms propose 50:50 assessment system and weighted marks
byline: A 50:50 assessment system combining continuous and summative assessments has been proposed under Sri Lanka’s new education reforms, the Education Ministry said.

title: Three seawater desalination projects currently under NWSDB
byline: Housing, Construction and Water Supply Minister Dr. Susil Ranasinghe said three seawater desalination projects are currently being implemented under the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB).

title: Migrant workers to get housing loans up to Rs.10m under ‘Ethera Diriya’ scheme
byline: Sri Lankan migrant workers will be eligible to obtain housing loans ranging from Rs.500,000 to Rs.10 million under the new “Ethera Diriya” Migrant Workers Housing Loan Scheme introduced by the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE).

title: 18 Air Force athletes join Sri Lanka contingent for 20th Asian Games
byline: Sri Lanka’s official sports contingent is scheduled to depart next Sunday (13) for the 20th Asian Games, which will begin on 19 September in Nagoya, Japan, with 18 athletes from the Sri Lanka Air Force (SLAF) among the 156 athletes representing the country.

title: Nearly 1,000 children diagnosed with cancer annually in Sri Lanka
byline: Between 900 and 1,000 children and young people aged from birth to 19 years are diagnosed with cancer in Sri Lanka every year, Community Medicine Specialist Dr. Suraj Perera said.

title: Sri Lanka exports first amphibious vessel to Europe
byline: Sri Lanka has exported its first high-tech amphibious vessel capable of operating both on land and at sea to Europe, marking a new milestone in the country’s naval manufacturing industry.

title: Government moves to cut paper use in Parliament
byline: The Government is taking steps to reduce paper usage in Parliament and the public sector through digitalisation, Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya said in Parliament today.

title: New education reforms to introduce 40-minute subject periods
byline: The new education reforms have proposed introducing 40-minute subject periods as part of changes to the general education system, according to the Education Ministry.

title: Death compensation for migrant workers increased to Rs.2 million
byline: Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath said compensation for Sri Lankan migrant workers who die while employed overseas has been increased from Rs.600,000 to Rs.2 million.

title: Oil shock weighs on CSE as ASPI falls for third straight session
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed lower for a third consecutive session on 10 September 2026, as escalating tensions in the Middle East and the sharp rise in global oil prices weighed on investor sentiment. Brent crude moved above USD 100 per barrel amid renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and heightened concerns over disruptions to regional energy supplies, adding to risk aversion across global markets.

title: Deepfake images used to target women political leaders: Prime Minister
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya today revealed that deepfake images are being used to target women political leaders in Sri Lanka, which poses a threat to democracy and the functioning of democracy.

title: No one can stop our September 12 campaign - Namal
byline: No one can stop our campaign, which is to be launched against the government starting September 12, SLPP MP Namal Rajapaksa said today.

title: CJ being blackmailed: Opposition MP
byline: Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena is being blackmailed by powerful persons in the government, Opposition MP Amila Prasad told Parliament today.

title: Algeria cuts diplomatic ties with the UAE
byline: Algeria abruptly severed diplomatic relations ​with the United Arab Emirates on Thursday, citing what it described as a series ‌of ’’provocative or hostile’’ actions by Abu Dhabi but giving no specific reason for the move.

title: Police hunt drug links behind Facebook parties
byline: The Inspector General of Police has launched a special intelligence operation to identify and monitor parties organized through Facebook, as well as the locations where such gatherings are held.

title: Houthis advance along Yemeni coast, threaten Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea
byline: Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen’s port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced down the ​Red Sea coast to strategic islands, military sources said, hours after President Donald Trump said he expected the Iran war to end after midterm elections.

title: Twenty-five dead after fire on cargo ship in eastern China
byline: Twenty-five people have been killed in a fire on a foreign-flagged cargo ship docked at a port in eastern China, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

title: ’He’s massive!’ Meet Hugo, the world’s tallest horse
byline: A Shire horse that has entered the record books as the world’s tallest living horse could exceed his height as he is still growing, his owner has said.
